samples.generated:
I went back to the <PLACE>. I had never seen the thing finished; but,
as I stood there with my friend, I imagined it finished. I saw a man in
the window, a man who would always be there when we passed by. But this
wasn’t the point. It was the man who was gone. The only living thing I
saw was the dead man. The other things were all empty. There was no
man in the shop windows; no boy at the street corners; no one in the
street except myself. I went down into the darkened streets of the city,
and I could see nobody there. The streets seemed to me to be empty like
the shops. There was nobody in the streets of <PLACE>. I was
looking for him when I met him. He came up suddenly out of the dust and
sand and looked at me with those eyes of his. Then we walked together,
the two men, the living man and the dead man.

samples.prompt: Write a philosophical essay contrasting two modes of reasoning: one that begins with first principles and fundamental purposes, and another that starts with immediate observations and works backward. Use an extended metaphor involving a common object to illustrate the difference between these approaches.
samples.generated:
The two methods can be easily illustrated by an imaginary comparison; for,
let us say, that there is a large and ornamental clock which stands on a
corner of the street. A man comes along and strikes the hour; a few
seconds pass; then he asks himself what the time is. In this way he
arrives at his conclusion. But in reality, the man would first ask
himself why he struck the hour; and then he would remember that the
clock was there; and then he would think of the long history of this
clock; and then he would consider the great mystery of time; and then
he would think of time as it is in all creation; and then he would come
to the conclusion that it was three o’clock.

The man who started with the immediate observation of the clock was a
practical man. He arrived at a practical conclusion; he had nothing more
to do than to walk out to buy some bread. The man who started with the
principles of the universe was a metaphysical man. He arrived at a
metaphysical conclusion; he had nothing more to do than to go back into
his room and write a book.
